challenges.says: Criterion 2 presumes 'another source choice is shown' and can be switched away from file picking, but criterion 3 says no folder or domain choice is offered at all, so the two contradict and the rule it cites (folder box enabled only with 'This folder') has no behaviour left to carry.

Criterion 3 states as fact that no Windows-folder choice is offered, while the first open question asks whether to offer the Windows policy definitions folder or the stored package; the criterion settles what the story says is undecided.

Criterion 6 cites base.decision-23, which only says uploads are checked for size and type before parsing; it cannot carry 'told what is missing' or the window staying open, which come from the dropped refusal part of the OK rule (businessrule-53176229115945924012), and the refusal text is left to an open question.

Criterion 4 (names appear in a list, list unchanged when the dialog is closed without picking) rests on no cited rule or decision; decision-1 says nothing of a file list, so the behaviour is invented, and the Browse action's own reading of the rule is not cited.

Criterion 1 cites businessrule-76226373219464614800 only for 'first choice selected' and drops its stated condition that the SYSVOL choice exists only when the computer is on a domain and the folder is found; that condition is not covered by any criterion (decision-7 is cited only for the Active Directory lookup of a GPO's POL file, not for definitions folders).
